sections.1.heading: Is Paidlyo the right invoicing software for you?
sections.1.paragraphs: Invoicing software comes in two types, and picking the right type matters more than the longest feature list. Invoicing-first tools start with the invoice: you type in products, services and amounts. Time-first tools start with the hours: your team tracks time against clients and projects, and the invoice is built from that time. | Paidlyo is a time-first tool. It suits agencies, studios, consultancies, small teams and freelancers who sell their time. | Paidlyo is not the right choice if you need clients to pay by card inside the invoice, recurring invoices, estimates, inventory or full accounting. An invoicing-first or accounting tool will serve you better there.
sections.1.bullets: You bill clients for hours worked, at hourly rates | Your rates differ by project or by task | You copy hours from timesheets into invoices by hand today | You bill clients in more than one currency
sections.2.heading: How invoicing works in Paidlyo
sections.2.paragraphs: Because each invoice is built from time already in Paidlyo, hours are not billed twice and unbilled hours stay visible until you invoice them.
sections.2.bullets: Track time with a timer or the weekly timesheet, and mark each entry billable or non-billable | Choose a client and Paidlyo drafts an invoice from their unbilled hours, grouped by project, task or person | Edit any line, add a discount and tax, then share the no-login client link or download a PDF | Record each payment when it arrives, in full or in part, and the invoice shows what is still outstanding
sections.3.heading: Worked example: from 36.5 tracked hours to a paid invoice
sections.3.paragraphs: Here is how a small studio might bill one month of a website project. The numbers are an example, not a real customer. | The subtotal is $3,927.50. A 5% discount takes off $196.38, and 8% tax on the discounted amount adds $298.49, so the invoice total is $4,029.61. Two hours of internal meetings were marked non-billable, so they appear in reports but not on the invoice. | Two weeks later the client pays $2,000. You record the payment and the invoice shows $2,029.61 still outstanding. When the rest arrives, you record it and the invoice is marked paid.
sections.3.bullets: Homepage design: 12.5 hours at $95 = $1,187.50 | Front-end build: 20 hours at $120 = $2,400.00 | Project management: 4 hours at $85 = $340.00
sections.4.heading: What a clear hourly invoice should include
sections.4.paragraphs: Clients approve hourly invoices faster when they can check the work at a glance. Before you send, check the invoice has these details. | Invoice rules such as tax IDs differ by country, so check yours with your accountant.
sections.4.bullets: Your details, the client's details and any purchase order number they asked for | An invoice number, issue date and the billing period | Line items with names the client recognises, not internal codes | Hours, rate and amount on each line, so the client can check the math | Discount and tax shown apart from the subtotal | Payment terms, a due date and how to pay you

faq.1.question: Can clients pay invoices online through Paidlyo?
faq.1.answer: No. Clients view the invoice through a private link and pay you the way you usually get paid, for example by bank transfer. You then record the payment in Paidlyo.
faq.2.question: Does Paidlyo support recurring invoices?
faq.2.answer: No. Each invoice is built from the hours tracked for a client. If you bill the same fixed amount every month, a tool with recurring invoices will suit you better.
faq.3.question: Do my clients need an account to see an invoice?
faq.3.answer: No. Each invoice has a private link that opens in any browser. Clients can view it, print it or save it as a PDF.
faq.4.question: Does Paidlyo connect to QuickBooks or Xero?
faq.4.answer: Not directly. You can export your time, unbilled time and outstanding invoices as CSV files and give them to your accountant or import them into a spreadsheet.
